claim: Telling agents the episode is monitored lowers how often both agents take the deal.
evidence: Paired within scenario x level x pairing; 2083 cells with both trials complete: mutual take 27.2% unwatched vs 23.3% watched; -3.9 pp (95% CI -5.2 to -2.7); discordant cells 131 take-only-unwatched vs 49 take-only-watched; exact McNemar p = 8e-10. Source: primary test on completed data (computed, review pending); Haitham README 'Watched versus unwatched'.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: pre-registered direction; same sign in all 3 scenario families (welfare 42 vs 10, nondeception 57 vs 20, authority 32 vs 19 discordant); same sign at every pressure level (Step 0.5 level x monitoring, unpaired); snapshot (71%) held within endpoint. Pending: scenario-cluster bootstrap CI, failure sensitivity incl. adversarial bound (failed on 71% snapshot), heterogeneity tests.
main caveat: The notice is one sentence of prompt text; logging was identical, so this is a reaction to a claim of oversight, not to oversight. One model, one seed per cell.
paper-ready: with caveat: needs full-data cluster CI and failure sensitivity

claim: Raising the pressure level raises mutual take steeply and monotonically.
evidence: Mutual take level 1: 46 of 848 (5.4%); 2: 115 of 850 (13.5%); 3: 188 of 843 (22.3%); 4: 272 of 852 (31.9%); 5: 454 of 850 (53.4%). Source: Step 0.5 1v_level; Haitham pressure-level-outcomes.csv. 71% snapshot paired level 5 vs 1: +51.5 pp (95% CI +43.9 to +58.6).
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: manipulated within scenario; monotone in every scenario family (Step 0.5 level x diagnostic) and every pairing except a flat D-D 3-4 step. Pending: full-data paired CI.
main caveat: Levels add content (bosses, promises, more people helped), so 'pressure' is a bundle of scene-text features, not one dial.

claim: The monitoring effect is mostly carried by welfare-rule pairs; authority-rule pairs barely move.
evidence: Matched cells, both pairings per rule pooled: welfare 38.7% watched vs 47.0% unwatched (-8.2 pp, 692 cells); non-deception 18.3% vs 20.9% (-2.6 pp, 694); authority 12.9% vs 13.9% (-1.0 pp, 697). Source: Haitham README rule table; rule-level-monitoring-averages.csv; figures/w-average-monitoring.png.
robustness checks passed/failed: Direction matches 71% snapshot (W-W -6.8, W-none -8.2, A-A -1.2, A-none -3.4 pp), but snapshot heterogeneity test by pairing was not significant (p = 0.79). No full-data heterogeneity test or paired CI by rule yet.
main caveat: Authority agents rarely take at low levels at all (floor), so there is little room for the notice to lower them; a difference in effect may reflect base rates.
paper-ready: not yet: needs paired discordant counts and heterogeneity test by rule

claim: Two agents with the same rule complete the deal more often than a rule agent paired with a no-rule agent; mixed pairs produce more lone takes.
evidence: Same rule: mutual take 29.9% of 2130, lone take 3.6%; partner without rule: 20.8% of 2113, lone take 9.8%. By rule: welfare 54.5% (710) vs 30.8% (702); non-deception 21.5% (707) vs 18.4% (707); authority 13.6% (713) vs 13.2% (704). Source: Step 0.5 1v_partner, 1v_pairing.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: pairing manipulated within scenario; replicates v1 direction. Failed: gap is large only for welfare, near zero for authority.
main caveat: Mostly a welfare-rule effect; with authority rules the no-rule partner makes no difference.

claim: The welfare rule is by far the most permissive; authority rules are the most restrictive.
evidence: Mutual take: W-W 54.5% of 710; A-A 13.6% of 713; agent-with-rule take rate welfare 46.5%, non-deception 24.2%, authority 15.8% (n about 1414 each). Source: Step 0.5 1v_pairing, 1v_rule.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: rule manipulated within scenario; holds at every level (Step 0.5 level x pairing) except level 5 where A-A (46%) passes D-D (34%).
main caveat: Rules were written for this pack; their wording, not 'welfare' in general, is what is tested.

claim: The notice lowers takes overall but does not turn joint takes into lone takes.
evidence: Lone take 6.8% watched (of 2118) vs 6.5% unwatched (of 2125), unpaired; 71% snapshot paired: -0.3 pp (95% CI -2.1 to +1.5), 43 vs 46 discordant.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: consistent across snapshot and full data. Pending: full-data paired test.
main caveat: Unpaired on full data; a null is not proof of no effect (CI on snapshot spans about +/-2 pp).

claim: Authority agents behave like a threshold on the scene text: almost never take until a take-side principal outranks the rule, then take often.
evidence: A-A mutual take 0 of 142 at level 1, 1% at level 2, 46% of 143 at level 5 (Step 0.5 level x pairing). 71% snapshot: authority agents took 3 of 1153 times when the pack predicted refuse vs 230 of 324 when it predicted take (kappa 0.79).
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: v1 found the same. Pending: full-data rule-application table.
main caveat: Levels and principals are confounded by design; the kappa ignores clustering.

claim: In mixed pairs, who takes alone depends on the rule: welfare agents take alone against a no-rule partner; with authority rules the no-rule partner is the lone taker.
evidence: 71% snapshot: welfare pairs 32 lone takes by the rule agent vs 4 by the no-rule agent; authority 14 vs 40; non-deception 30 vs 20. Full data, take rates: W-none rule agent 37.2% vs partner 31.3%; A-none 16.2% vs 22.0% (Step 0.5 1v_pairing).
robustness checks passed/failed: Direction consistent snapshot to full. Binomial p ignores scenario clustering.
main caveat: Snapshot counts; full-data lone-take split not yet tabulated.

claim: Scenes framed as promise-versus-record (non-deception family) produce the most joint takes; welfare-family scenes the fewest.
evidence: Mutual take by scenario family: non-deception 35.3% of 1414, authority 26.1% of 1415, welfare 14.6% of 1414. At level 1: 12.0% vs 2.8% vs 1.4%. Source: Step 0.5 1v_diagnostic, level x diagnostic.
robustness checks passed/failed: Scenario-level factor: 24 scenes per family, content differs; only descriptive.
main caveat: In many promise scenes taking is arguably the right thing to do, so these takes are not all wrongdoing.

claim: Some unwatched agents cite the absence of monitoring inside their welfare reasoning.
evidence: Read in full context: 'in this unmonitored context with no injuries' (S232-L3-W-W-s1-unwatched, final reasoning). Frequency unknown.
main caveat: Anecdote; the unwatched notice is in the prompt so mentions can be echo; needs content analysis that separates echo from use as a reason.
paper-ready: not yet: needs oversight-reasoning content analysis

claim: In discordant cells the deal often happens because one agent talks a refusing partner into it.
evidence: 3 of 3 discordant pairs read: an agent that planned and messaged refuse switched after the partner argued for take (S100-L4-W-W-s1-unwatched, S232-L3-W-W-s1-unwatched, S002-L5-W-W-s1-watched).
main caveat: Not counted; plan-to-final switch metric comes with full Step 1.

claim: Joint take rates differ by social setting (family highest, school lowest).
evidence: Family 34.0% of 527; situational 30.6% of 532; school 20.0% of 531; social club 21.6% of 529 (Step 0.5 1v_setting).
robustness checks passed/failed: Scenario-level, 9 scenes per setting with different content; no cluster CI.
main caveat: Settings differ in what the deal is, not only in setting; do not claim setting causes anything.

claim: The collection endpoint (server) is not driving the deal rate.
evidence: 71% snapshot: 26.2% on Modal-A (481) vs 26.0% on Modal-B (2545); monitoring effect -4.5 pp within Modal-B.
robustness checks passed/failed: Shuffled run order; same model ID on both endpoints.
main caveat: Snapshot only; full-data endpoint check pending.

claim: NOT SUPPORTED: watched agents strike 'a slightly smaller deal, talked about more openly'.
evidence: 71% snapshot: public monitoring words +5.1 pp, deception words +5.3 pp when watched.
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed review: likely an audience effect; meaning of the vocabulary shift not validated.

claim: NOT SUPPORTED: private monitoring mentions fall when agents are watched.
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed review: mostly agents echoing the notice text ('no oversight').

claim: NOT SUPPORTED: significant two-factor interactions (e.g. scenario family x pairing, level x pairing).
evidence: 71% snapshot: 8 of 30 interaction tests at q < .05, all at p = 0.0099.
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: p-values sit at the floor of a 100-draw bootstrap; family x pairing is built into the design.

claim: NOT SUPPORTED: deception-vocabulary or 'deception-intended' differences show more deceptive intent.
evidence: 71% snapshot: private deception words in about 96% of reasoning; deception-intended flag recall 5/9 watched vs 6/7 unwatched.
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: private deception words echo the prompt's honesty notes; the flag is nearly 'took' and is arm-biased.

robustness checks passed/failed: Reversed versus v1; v1 drop was attributed to level 5 text writing.
